title: spec-gate v0: the first trusted judge
description:
## Goal

`spec-gate` v0: the first trusted judge. It runs `spec-gate-specs` against a `spec-gate` commit, refuses a scenario never seen red, fails on skipped or undefined steps and on zero scenarios, and refuses to run when its own checksum differs from the pin. Everything else in `docs/design.md` is out of v0.

Design: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate/docs/design.md` (§8 dog-fooding, §10 decisions). Specs: `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate-specs`.

## In scope (criteria in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.req.md`)

- `sg-dop.1`, `sg-dop.2`: the verdict names product and spec commits; the spec version is chosen by the spec repository.
- `sg-397.1`–`.3`: red-first.
- `sg-zf8.1`, `sg-zf8.2`: undefined step and zero scenarios fail the run.
- `sg-i86.1`: checksum refusal.

## Out of scope

- `sg-3zr.*` (binding check; owned by `binding-contract`, D-24).
- `sg-ubq.*` (local vs authoritative runs; needs the runner, D-16).
- `sg-212.1` (full agent report).
- Holdout, mutation, structure, purity and contract stages; the runner host; commit statuses.

## Separation (D-11)

The spec-side work (DSL, driver port, CLI driver, acceptance harness, in `spec-gate-specs`) and the product work (`spec-gate` itself) are done in separate tasks by separate agent sessions. The agent that implements `spec-gate` never edits `spec-gate-specs`, and spec-side changes reach `main` only by operator merge (D-09, D-14).

## Success Criteria

- Every in-scope criterion's scenario was seen failing against a `spec-gate` commit before v0, and passes against v0.
- The acceptance harness was seen failing on a deliberately undefined step.
- The operator has reviewed v0, signed tag `v0`, and pinned its sha256 in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.toml`.

## Operator decision

> "accept all" — operator, 2026-10-21, accepting the recommendations for D-01 to D-25 as recorded in `docs/design.md` §10.

> "commit both and file the v0 epic" — operator, 2026-10-21.

Approves: the 25 decisions as worded in `docs/design.md` §10, including the follow-up work `spec-gate mint` (D-20) and extending `binding-contract` to read Gherkin tags (D-24); filing this epic. Nothing else is approved: no edits to `~/code/tools`, no gate or lint configuration changes, no changes to requirements or scenarios except agent drafts merged by the operator (D-15), and no scope beyond the in-scope list above.

## Flagged assumptions (operator to confirm)

- **`spec-gate mint` is in v0.** D-19 lists v0 as "acceptance, red-first, checksum refusal, nothing else", but red-first keys its ledger on minted `@id` tags (D-20), and ids are never written by hand. This epic assumes mint is part of red-first. Alternative: v0 keys the ledger on something else, which contradicts D-20.
- **Seed reds are recorded before v0 exists.** The seed scenarios must be seen red before the judge that records reds exists. This epic assumes the operator records them from a harness run against a pre-v0 `spec-gate` commit, in the ledger format v0 defines, and that this recording is part of the bootstrap review (D-19).

title: Draft the scenario-id minting requirement and scenarios in spec-gate-specs
description:
## What

Draft the requirement and scenarios for scenario-id minting in `spec-gate-specs`, as an agent draft for operator merge (D-15, D-20).

`spec-gate mint` assigns an `@id:<hashid>` tag to every scenario lacking one, never overwrites an existing id, and never reuses one; uniqueness is decided against every feature file in the repository. Follow `req`'s minting rules (`~/code/tools/req/SPEC.md`, "IDS") and the house spec style (`~/kbe/guides/writing-specifications.md`: EARS, witness and near-miss).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The requirement is in `spec-gate.req.md` with ids minted by `req mint`; `req check` is clean.
- Each new criterion has one scenario tagged `@covers:`.
- Delivered as a branch or PR on `spec-gate-specs`; nothing reaches `main` without operator merge.

title: Acceptance harness, DSL and CLI driver in spec-gate-specs
description:
## What

The executable side of `spec-gate-specs`: the DSL, driver port, CLI driver and `cucumber` acceptance harness that run the v0 in-scope scenarios against a `spec-gate` binary. Layout and rules: `docs/design.md` §3 and §10 (D-01 to D-04, D-06 to D-08, D-11, D-23).

- The DSL has its own vocabulary and does not depend on `spec-gate`'s crates (D-02).
- The CLI driver builds fixture spec and product repositories in a temporary directory and observes exit codes, report and ledger bytes; it never reaches into `spec-gate` internals.
- The CLI driver carries a self-test against a fake `spec-gate` that lies; the driver must detect the lie (D-11).
- `hex-lint` roles from the first commit; the layering `acceptance → dsl → driver-port ← driver-cli` is a build failure when broken.
- `fail_on_skipped` on, and seen failing once on a deliberately undefined step.

Done by an agent session that does not implement `spec-gate` itself (D-11).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Against a `spec-gate` commit with no v0 implementation, every in-scope scenario runs and fails for the stated reason (not a harness error).
- The undefined-step check and the lying-fake self-test were each seen red, then green.
- `hex-lint` passes and was seen failing on a planted forbidden edge.
- Delivered as a branch or PR on `spec-gate-specs` for operator merge.

title: Implement spec-gate v0
description:
## What

`spec-gate` v0 in `~/IdeaProjects/spec-gate`: the CLI that makes the in-scope scenarios pass. Judge a product commit against spec `main` and name both in the verdict; keep the red-first ledger and refuse a scenario never seen red; record a red (`spec-gate red`); mint scenario ids (`spec-gate mint`); fail on skipped or undefined steps and on zero scenarios; refuse to run when its own checksum differs from `[judge] sha256`.

Architecture per `~/kbe/guides/rust-native-architecture-template.md`: functional core (ledger rules, verdict computation as pure functions), effects at the edges, `hex-lint` and `effect-audit` clean.

Done by an agent session that does not edit `spec-gate-specs` (D-11). The agent reads the specs from a read-only checkout and runs the harness locally for feedback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every in-scope scenario passes when the harness in `spec-gate-specs` runs against this commit.
- Unit tests at the ports with fake adapters; property tests (`hegeltest`) on the ledger rules.
- `cargo mutants` on the changed code; survivors triaged with `mutation-triage`.
- `hex-lint` and `effect-audit` pass.

title: Operator bootstrap: record seed reds, review, tag and pin v0
description:
## What

Operator bootstrap of the first judge (D-19). Not agent work.

1. Record the seed reds: the harness run against a pre-v0 `spec-gate` commit, in the ledger format v0 defines.
2. Review v0 by hand.
3. Sign tag `v0`; build with `cargo build --release --locked`; compute sha256.
4. Set `[judge] sha256` in `spec-gate-specs/spec-gate.toml`; merge.
5. Run the seed scenarios with v0 once; record the result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Ledger holds a red before the first green for every in-scope scenario.
- `spec-gate.toml` pins v0's sha256, and v0 refuses to run with a tampered pin.
